messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: infra-oncall paged — Node provisioning errors: high rate of image pull failures for GPU images. Incident created: 1795012345
eli: acked. Seeing kubelet failures during bootstrap across several clusters. New nodes stuck in ContainerCreating.
sara: what's the exact error? 429 vs 401?
eli: mainly 429 Too Many Requests from Docker Hub edge mirrors, plus occasional 401 token expired when hitting auth proxy. Sample: "error pulling image configuration: received unexpected HTTP status: 429 Too Many Requests"
raj: confirmed. Bootstrap uses docker.io/nvidia/cuda:11.8-runtime. Some pulls get rate-limited by Docker Hub; others succeed via cached proxy.
joanne: any end-user impact yet? Which customers?
eli: impact limited to provisioning — autoscaler cannot finish node joins so some Dedicated clusters waiting for extra capacity. No running pods OOM/killed yet.
sara: check docker hub status and any CDN mirrors
eli: docker status page shows partial rate limiting incident (link posted). Also seeing bursty request rates from our fleets.
raj: mitigation proposal: 1) pause autoscaler 2) fallback bootstrap to registry.internal.redwood 3) pre-pull images via DaemonSet 4) bake AMI with images
janet: agree. Pause autoscaling to avoid noisy retries. We'll take a controlled approach.
eli: running these now:
```
kubectl -n kube-system annotate deploy/cluster-autoscaler redwood.io/autoscaler-paused=true --overwrite
kubectl apply -f https://git.internal.redwood/prepull/gpu-cuda-daemonset.yaml
```
raj: opened ticket with Docker Hub (INC-987654) and attached pull logs/timestamps.
eli: also pinged NVIDIA to confirm direct docker pulls vs proxy behavior.
sara: I'm building a pre-baked AMI with the cuda runtime baked in (est ~10-15m). If successful we can prefer that AMI for immediate launches.
joanne: drafting customer-facing message. Draft: "We're seeing delays in GPU node provisioning due to third-party registry rate limits for GPU runtime images. Engineers have applied an internal cache fallback and are pre-warming capacity. No running workloads affected. We'll update with ETA."
raj: applying internal fallback in bootstrap scripts now — overriding image repo to registry.internal.redwood/nvidia/cuda:11.8-runtime when ENV VAR USE_INTERNAL_REG=1
eli: also deploying a small helper DaemonSet to pre-pull & cache layers on healthy hosts that'll serve as pull-proxy for new nodes if needed.
janet: handoff note — I'm taking oncall for the next shift in 20m. Eli/raj please leave clear playbook steps and current state.
eli: handoff summary to include:
- cause: Docker Hub rate-limiting + edge auth token expiry causing pulls of nvidia/cuda images to fail
- impact: delayed provisioning for Dedicated GPU pools; some customer clusters waiting for capacity expansions; no running pod terminations
- actions taken: autoscaler paused, internal registry fallback enabled, DaemonSet pre-pulls applied, AMI bake started, Docker Hub ticket opened
- next steps: finish AMI bake, validate node join with baked AMI, unpause autoscaler once pre-warmed, consider permanent caching/mirroring and bootstrap circuit-breaker
raj: AMI bake completed: ami-0f1e2d3c. Updated GPU launch config to prefer new AMI.
sara: monitoring — image_pull_latency and image_pull_errors down after enabling internal fallback; still watching for residual token errors.
joanne: posted to status.redwood.com and notified customers with recent provisioning activity. Updated message includes link to this thread.
janet: noted follow-ups: eng-infra to add periodic AMI bakes for critical GPU images, add retry/circuit-breaker logic to bootstrap, and expand pre-warm pool for Dedicated.
eli: small note — our external APM struggled to ingest some of the image-pull metrics during the outage; correlate with our host-side metrics as well.
joanne: thanks. I'll keep customer comms open. Will escalate to account reps for affected enterprise tenants.
incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED: 1795012345 -> status: mitigated (third-party registry rate-limiting). Postmortem assigned to eng-infra. Last updated 1795014120
